plan.chapterName: OpenStax Calculus, chapter 12: Vectors in Space
plan.contextChunk: This figure is a three-dimensional construction drawn in the first octant that locates a single point three different ways at once. The vertical axis is labeled z, the axis running to the right is labeled y, and the axis coming toward the viewer at the lower left is labeled x. A filled black dot at the upper right is tagged by two stacked lines of text, P(x, y, z) on top and P(rho, theta, phi) beneath it. A solid blue segment runs from the origin out to the dot and is labeled rho along its length. A small arc near the origin between the z-axis and that segment is labeled phi. Dashed orange lines complete the rest of the construction: a vertical drop from the point down to the xy-plane labeled z, and a segment from the origin across the xy-plane to the foot of that drop labeled r, with a small square where they meet marking the right angle. A second arc at the origin, between the x-axis and the segment r, is labeled theta. Superimposing all three descriptions on one point exposes theta and r as the quantities the systems share. The drawing introduces the ordered triple (rho, theta, phi), in which one distance and two angles fix a location in space.

elements: z-axis: vertical line through origin with arrowhead at top, label 'z' at the tip
y-axis: line from origin toward screen-right with arrowhead, label 'y' below the tip
x-axis: line from origin toward the lower-left (coming at the viewer) with arrowhead, label 'x' at the tip
origin at the common intersection of the three axes, positioned left-of-center and low in the frame
filled black dot for point P, high and to the right, above the y-axis region
two stacked text labels to the upper right of the dot: 'P(x, y, z)' on top, 'P(ρ, θ, φ)' beneath
solid blue segment from origin to P, labeled 'ρ' in blue at its midpoint (slightly above the line)
small arc at the origin spanning from the z-axis to the blue ρ segment, with arrowhead, labeled 'φ'
dashed orange vertical segment dropping from P straight down to its foot Q in the xy-plane, labeled 'z' in orange to the right of the segment
dashed orange segment from the origin across the xy-plane to the foot Q, labeled 'r' in orange at its midpoint
small square right-angle marker at Q where the vertical drop meets the xy-plane segment
small arc at the origin in the xy-plane spanning from the x-axis to the dashed r segment, with arrowhead, labeled 'θ'
optional faint projection segments to the x- and y-axes used by the rectangular readout

interactions.teaches: ρ is the straight-line distance from the origin to P: growing it slides P outward along a fixed ray, stretching the blue segment while both angles stay put
interactions.label: ρ (distance from origin)

interactions.teaches: θ swings the whole vertical triangle around the z-axis; the ground projection r rotates in the xy-plane while ρ, φ and the height z are unchanged — the angle shared with cylindrical coordinates
interactions.label: θ (from +x-axis, in xy-plane)

interactions.teaches: φ is measured down from the +z-axis: small φ lifts P toward the z-axis and shrinks r, φ = 90° lays P flat in the xy-plane where z = 0
interactions.label: φ (from +z-axis)

interactions.teaches: the same fixed point has three descriptions; switching highlights which pieces belong to which system and exposes θ and z as shared quantities, with r = ρ sin φ linking cylindrical to spherical
interactions.label: Readout

interactions.teaches: that the dashed r segment really lies flat in the xy-plane and the drop to it is vertical — the right-angle marker is genuine 3D structure, not a drawing convention

demo_steps.title: The spherical triple
demo_steps.narration: One distance ρ and two angles θ and φ pin down P. The blue segment is ρ, the arc at the z-axis is φ, and the arc in the floor is θ.

demo_steps.title: Stretch ρ
demo_steps.narration: Increasing ρ pushes P straight out along the same ray. Both angles are untouched, so the direction is fixed and only the distance changes.

demo_steps.title: Swing θ
demo_steps.narration: θ rotates the entire triangle about the z-axis. The height z and the ground distance r stay the same — P traces a horizontal circle.

demo_steps.title: Tip φ toward the pole
demo_steps.narration: Shrinking φ tilts ρ up toward the z-axis: the dashed r collapses while the dashed z grows, since r = ρ sin φ and z = ρ cos φ.

demo_steps.title: Same point, cylindrical
demo_steps.narration: Hold the point still and read it as (r, θ, z). The orange ground segment and orange vertical drop are now the featured quantities — θ is carried over unchanged from spherical.

demo_steps.title: Same point, rectangular
demo_steps.narration: Finally read it as (x, y, z): r splits into x = r cos θ and y = r sin θ, while z is the same vertical drop all three systems share.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: World scale: axes span roughly 0 to 6 units positive with a short negative stub (~0.4) behind the origin; z-axis drawn to ~6 up, y-axis to ~6 screen-right, x-axis to ~5 toward the viewer's lower-left. Origin sits low-left in the frame (roughly 25% across, 30% up) so the point P lands high-right. Axis mapping: +Y world = screen-up = the 'z' label; +X world = screen-right = the 'y' label; +Z world = receding toward viewer lower-left = the 'x' label. Formulas: r = ρ sin φ, z = ρ cos φ, x = r cos θ = ρ sin φ cos θ, y = r sin θ = ρ sin φ sin θ; ρ = √(x²+y²+z²), tan θ = y/x, cos φ = z/ρ. Defaults ρ = 5, θ = 65°, φ = 60° give r ≈ 4.33, z ≈ 2.50, x ≈ 1.83, y ≈ 3.92 — matching the source where P sits well to the right (large y), only slightly forward (small x), and about half the height of the ρ segment. Colors: axes and axis labels black (#000000) with solid arrowheads; ρ segment solid blue (#1F5C8B, ~3px) with blue 'ρ' label placed above the segment's midpoint; r and z construction lines dashed orange (#E8622A, ~2px, dash ~0.18/gap 0.12) with matching orange italic labels 'r' (below the ground segment's midpoint) and 'z' (right of the vertical drop); φ arc black, radius ~0.9 from origin, swept from the z-axis clockwise to the ρ segment with a small arrowhead, label 'φ' just left of the arc; θ arc black/orange, radius ~0.8 in the xy-plane, swept from the +x-axis to the r segment, label 'θ' between x-axis and r; right-angle square at foot Q, side ~0.3, lying in the vertical plane containing r and the drop. Point P is a black sphere of radius ~0.09; its two text labels sit to the upper-right of the dot, left-aligned and stacked with 'P(x, y, z)' above 'P(ρ, θ, φ)'. Highlight colors for the toggle: rectangular emphasizes x/y/z projection segments in a neutral gray-green, cylindrical emphasizes the orange r and z, spherical emphasizes the blue ρ plus both arcs.
interactionPlan.notes: Use an orthographic camera in a standard isometric-style pose with a white background so the figure reads as a clean line drawing. Draw all lines with Line2/LineMaterial (screen-space width) so thicknesses stay constant under orbit; dashed segments via LineDashedMaterial with computeLineDistances(), or Line2 dashed. Axis arrowheads as small ConeGeometry meshes. Arcs built from EllipseCurve points: the θ arc lies in the world XZ ground plane, the φ arc lies in the vertical plane containing the z-axis and ρ (rebuild or re-orient it whenever θ changes). All text labels as CSS2DRenderer sprites so they stay upright and crisp while orbiting; italic serif for the math symbols ρ, θ, φ, r, z. Rebuild only the point position, the three segments, the two arcs, and the right-angle square on slider change — keep geometry in preallocated buffers and update positions rather than re-instantiating. Clamp the visuals gracefully at φ = 0 and 180° (r → 0, hide the θ arc and the right-angle square) and at ρ = 0. Toggle should crossfade element opacity/color rather than add or remove geometry, so the point visibly stays fixed while the described quantities change. Add a small live numeric readout panel showing the active triple to three significant figures.

authoredContext:
In the spherical coordinate system, a point P in space (the figure) is represented by the ordered triple (ρ,θ,φ) where

In the Cartesian coordinate system, the location of a point in space is described using an ordered triple in which each coordinate represents a distance. In the cylindrical coordinate system, location of a point in space is described using two distances (randz) and an angle measure (θ). In the spherical coordinate system, we again use an ordered triple to describe the location of a point in space. In this case, the triple describes one distance and two angles. Spherical coordinates make it simple to describe a sphere, just as cylindrical coordinates make it easy to describe a cylinder. Grid lines for spherical coordinates are based on angle measures, like those for polar coordinates.

The relationship among spherical, rectangular, and cylindrical coordinates.

This figure is the first quadrant of the 3-dimensional coordinate system. It has a point labeled “(x, y, z) = (rho, theta, phi).” There is a line segment from the origin to the point. It is labeled “rho.” The angle between this line segment and the z-axis is phi. There is a line segment in the x y-plane from the origin to the shadow of the point. This segment is labeled “r.” The angle between the x-axis and r is theta.

By convention, the origin is represented as (0,0,0) in spherical coordinates.

Spherical coordinates of a point
Readout / highlight
Guided tour
Drag in the figure to orbit: the dashed r really lies flat in the xy-plane and the drop to it is truly vertical.
⚠ Figure failed to load

discrepancies: Camera/view: the initial viewpoint foreshortens the ρ direction so severely that the blue ρ segment renders as a short stub (~76 px) near the origin, whereas in the source ρ is the dominant long diagonal reaching the upper-right corner of the figure; the whole construction collapses into a small cluster around O.

Axis screen orientation differs from the source: the source draws the y-axis essentially horizontal to the right with x dropping steeply to the lower-left, while the generated figure uses a symmetric isometric-style view with both x and y at ~30° below horizontal, changing the recognizable layout.

The dashed orange r, the vertical z drop and the right-angle square are rendered at reduced opacity (0.45) in the default spherical mode, so they read as faint pale-orange hairlines instead of the clear, prominent dashed red-orange triangle that dominates the lower right of the source.
Because of the compressed projection, the φ, ρ and θ labels pile up in a tiny region next to the origin rather than being spread along their respective arcs/segments as in the source.
Extra gray-green projection segments and x/y projection labels (rectangular mode) exist beyond the source content, though they are hidden by default.
evaluation.notes: Mathematically correct and richly interactive (ρ/θ/φ sliders, coordinate-system toggle, 6-step guided tour, click-for-info), but the chosen viewpoint foreshortens ρ almost along the view axis so the main blue segment and the orange r/z triangle shrink to a cramped cluster at the origin, losing the open, easily-read composition of the source.

feedback.rationale: The concept and interaction structure are correct; the issues are concrete rendering fixes—camera orientation/scale, opacity of the dashed r/z triangle, and label placement—so the generator should adjust the implementation.

interactions.teaches: ρ is the straight-line distance from the origin to P: growing it slides P outward along a fixed ray, stretching the blue segment while both angles stay put
interactions.label: ρ (distance from origin)

interactions.teaches: θ swings the whole vertical triangle around the z-axis; the ground projection r rotates in the xy-plane while ρ, φ and the height z are unchanged — the angle shared with cylindrical coordinates
interactions.label: θ (from +x-axis, in xy-plane)

interactions.teaches: φ is measured down from the +z-axis: small φ lifts P toward the z-axis and shrinks r, φ = 90° lays P flat in the xy-plane where z = 0
interactions.label: φ (from +z-axis)

interactions.teaches: the same fixed point has three descriptions; switching highlights which pieces belong to which system and exposes θ and z as shared quantities, with r = ρ sin φ linking cylindrical to spherical
interactions.label: Readout

interactions.teaches: that the dashed r segment really lies flat in the xy-plane and the drop to it is vertical — the right-angle marker is genuine 3D structure, not a drawing convention

demo_steps.title: The spherical triple
demo_steps.narration: One distance ρ and two angles θ and φ pin down P. The blue segment is ρ, the arc at the z-axis is φ, and the arc in the floor is θ.

demo_steps.title: Stretch ρ
demo_steps.narration: Increasing ρ pushes P straight out along the same ray. Both angles are untouched, so the direction is fixed and only the distance changes.

demo_steps.title: Swing θ
demo_steps.narration: θ rotates the entire triangle about the z-axis. The height z and the ground distance r stay the same — P traces a horizontal circle.

demo_steps.title: Tip φ toward the pole
demo_steps.narration: Shrinking φ tilts ρ up toward the z-axis: the dashed r collapses while the dashed z grows, since r = ρ sin φ and z = ρ cos φ.

demo_steps.title: Same point, cylindrical
demo_steps.narration: Hold the point still and read it as (r, θ, z). The orange ground segment and orange vertical drop are now the featured quantities — θ is carried over unchanged from spherical.

demo_steps.title: Same point, rectangular
demo_steps.narration: Finally read it as (x, y, z): r splits into x = r cos θ and y = r sin θ, while z is the same vertical drop all three systems share.
